arguments.instructions: Purpose: find direct experimental evidence that adaptive gradient clipping (including AGC methods that scale clipping thresholds to parameter norms or adapt thresholds dynamically) reduces optimizer/training instability under noisy small-batch or high-gradient-variance training. Prioritize full-text empirical papers reporting divergence, loss spikes, NaNs, convergence stability, or performance versus no clipping/fixed clipping. Distinguish genuinely small-batch evidence from large-batch or unrelated robustness claims.

Purpose: find direct experimental evidence that adaptive gradient clipping (including AGC methods that scale clipping thresholds to parameter norms or adapt thresholds dynamically) reduces optimizer/training instability under noisy small-batch or high-gradient-variance training. Prioritize full-text empirical papers reporting divergence, loss spikes, NaNs, convergence stability, or performance versus no clipping/fixed clipping. Distinguish genuinely small-batch evidence from large-batch or unrelated robustness claims.

Purpose: identify conditions limiting the claim that adaptive gradient clipping reduces optimizer instability in noisy small-batch training. Search for empirical comparisons showing dependence on batch size, optimizer, architecture, clipping threshold, gradient noise, or cases where AGC is neutral/harmful; include foundational AGC papers if their actual experiments are not small-batch. Prioritize accessible full text and explicit ablations.
